name: Dale Nielsen
life: “My son learned the word tomorrow too early for my liking.” Monday often includes a stop at the blocks below Foundry Lofts, where Dale checks the little hand-lettered notices around Harbour Supply.
voice: My toddler kept moving it to save a seat for his dad. We told him the truth on the fourth visit.
appearance: Away from the heat of the kitchen, look for a brown corduroy jacket and a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. Dale has a round face with a pronounced chin, with a long plait tucked inside the collar. Dale folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing during a conversation.
personality: Dale has a strong competitive streak and a very soft spot for the person finishing last. A prize tastes better when everybody had enough time to enter.
agenda: To explain the pencil schedule to the child before the next appointment.
family: Nina Khan is Dale’s second cousin. Dale saves a place. Nina chooses whether to use it. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The kitchen without a boss*, Nina says, “I buy breakfast on a night wage. I want these new bosses to remember what two coins used to buy.”
connections: Cory Palmer. A saved seat and a child's game account for the mitten's first small journey. Also in the story is Astrid Reed (ward property worker).

reactions.situation: A patient wants the chair kept empty for a while
reactions.response: Dale saves the chair for a short agreed interval and checks who else needs it.
